title: Consolidate instrumentation contracts and add oracle metrics for console incident detection
creator: Ava Martinez
description: After a capacity/regression incident affecting Console routes, we discovered multiple blind spots: missing per-tenant oracle metrics (eviction-rate, queue-depth histograms), several key tracepoints were absent in the influx path, and dashboard panels used high-cardinality properties causing aggregation holes. This ticket consolidates instrumentation contracts (what every route/handler must emit), implements a small set of 'oracle' metrics for rapid incident triage, and produces a follow-up runbook and dashboard templates.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-10 we observed a prolonged runtime capacity regression affecting Console upload and insights queries. Initial paging and alerting were noisy; mean time to detect was ~42 minutes. The root postmortem identified missing per-tenant queue depth and eviction metrics as primary contributors to slow diagnosis, along with multiple dashboards that masked signal due to sampling and cardinality issues.
root_cause_analysis: 1) No standardized metric contract for console ingress and kv-cache subsystems: teams were emitting ad-hoc counters and tags. 2) Key tracepoints were not present in the insights pipeline (request lifecycle start/end, kv-eviction decision path), so traces lacked context to link latency spikes to eviction events. 3) Dashboards aggregated on free-form user_id and tenant_id without cardinality bucketing, causing aggregation blowups and time series omissions under load.
action_items: Define and publish an instrumentation contract doc (metric names, required labels, units, retention expectations) for Console handlers and KV cache — owner: Observability
Add 'oracle' metrics: per-tenant queue_depth (histogram buckets), kv_eviction_rate (per-minute gauge), request_backpressure_count — owner: Serving Runtime
Instrument tracepoints for request lifecycle boundary, kv-cache lookup/miss/hit, eviction decision, and autoscaler-boundary events — owner: Runtime Core
Replace free-form tenant/user tags in dashboards with bounded tenant_bucket tag (hash-prefix) and add cardinality guidance to dashboard templates — owner: Console UX
Create synthetic canary that exercises Console upload + insights flow every 5m and emits expected metrics for MTD — owner: SRE
Add alert rules tied to oracle metrics with clear runbook links and paging thresholds (e.g., queue_depth P99 > X for > 5m) — owner: SRE/Oncall

Retrofit existing high-entropy dashboards to use template variables and sampling rollups; add an automated lint check for new dashboards to prevent high cardinality panels — owner: Observability Tools
acceptance_criteria: Published instrumentation contract page in Confluence with examples and a JSON schema for metric exporters
Oracle metrics are emitted in production for top 25 tenants and visible in the metrics UI with dashboard panels
At least 5 missing tracepoints added and end-to-end traces can be used to correlate eviction events to request latency
New dashboard templates committed and used by Console team; automated dashboard lint prevents free-form tenant_id in future panels
Synthetic canary is green for 24h and triggers the new alert when artificially throttled in staging
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with Observability, Runtime, Console UX, SRE. Agreed on contract outline and oracle metric set.
2026-02-24: Initial PR adding queue_depth histogram and kv_eviction_rate gauge in runtime merged to staging: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842
2026-02-27: Tracing hooks prototype implemented for request boundary and kv-cache lookup; end-to-end traces visible in staging with correlation ids
2026-03-01: Dashboard template PR created and lint rule prototype added to observability-tools repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-tools/pull/91
review_feedback: PM review (Liam O'Connor): add customer examples showing why per-tenant metrics are necessary for enterprise SLAs
Design review (Maya Chen): dashboard templates should default to 1m rollups and provide an explainer tooltip for bucketed tenant view
Security review note (Ruth Gomez): metric labels must not include PII; confirm tenant_bucket hashing algorithm and document it
notes: Avoid introducing new high-cardinality labels. Recommend tenancy bucketing and a migration guide for teams emitting free-form tenant tags. Follow-up: run a 2-week audit to surface other dashboards with cardinality risks. If any customer-facing SLAs were impacted, coordinate messaging with Customer Success after acceptance criteria met.
